https://nineoclock.ro/romanias-capital-m.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Gabriel Avră mescu: Record Growth Signals a More Mature Financial Ecosystem By Dr. Adrian Leonard Mociulschi— Special for Nine O ’ Clock For years, Romania ’ s economic potential was easier to describe than to quantify. Today, the numbers are difficult to ignore. As investors worldwide search for stability, transparency, and growth in an uncertain environment, Romania ’ s capital market is attracting attention not merely as a regional exchange, but as an increasingly credible destination for investment and long-term capital formation. According to data presented by Gabriel Avrămescu, First Vice-President of the Financial Supervisory Authority ( ASF ), and publicly reported by AGERPRES, Romania’s benchmark BET Index has reached approximately 36,000 points, more than 80% above its level a year ago. Meanwhile, the market capitalization of the Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB) has risen to roughly RON 710 billion, an increase of 68% year-on-year. “In one year, the BET Index has broken threshold after threshold. We have reached a level of 36,000 points and recorded growth of more than 80% compared to the same period of the previous year,” Avrămescu said. These figures are notable not only because of their scale, but because of what they reveal about the evolution of Romania’s financial landscape. Strong market performance rarely emerges in isolation. It is often the product of deeper structural developments, including stronger institutions, expanding access to capital, and growing investor confidence. Central to this progress has been the Financial Supervisory Authority (ASF). While market rallies tend to capture headlines, sustainable growth depends on effective regulation, transparency, and investor protection. Predictable rules and credible oversight help create the confidence on which capital markets ultimately depend. The recent expansion of Romania’s capital market suggests that these foundations are becoming increasingly robust. The Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB) has been equally important in shaping this trajectory. Over the past decade, it has evolved beyond its traditional role as a trading venue, increasingly positioning itself as a platform for capital formation. By connecting investors with businesses seeking funding, BVB has helped strengthen Romania’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. Initiatives such as BVB Arena reflect a broader effort to bring growth-oriented companies closer to the capital markets. Another indicator highlighted by Avrămescu is the continued expansion of Romania’s investor base. The number of investors has now surpassed 325,000, a record for the local market. More importantly, this trend points to the emergence of a stronger investment culture, increasingly oriented toward long-term wealth creation rather than short-term speculation. Yet Avrămescu regards the current achievements as a milestone rather than a destination. “We believe this is only an intermediate level, and I consider that the potential offered by the Stock Exchange and by attracting investors is much greater,” he noted. Part of that future potential may come from the planned launch of a dedicated Growth Market for small and medium-sized enterprises. According to Avrămescu, the authorization process is already at an advanced stage. “We believe that this growth market represents a bridge between entrepreneurship and the capital market,” he explained. The initiative could provide Romanian SMEs with improved access to financing while offering investors new opportunities to participate in the growth of emerging businesses. In advanced economies, capital markets serve not only as investment mechanisms but also as engines of innovation, productivity, and economic modernization. Romania appears increasingly determined to strengthen that role. The recent milestones achieved by Romania’s capital market are more than headline-grabbing statistics. They point to the gradual strengthening of the financial infrastructure needed to support future growth. For international investors, the message is becoming increasingly clear: Romania is no longer merely a market of promise. It is becoming a market of performance, where institutions, investors, and companies are translating potential into measurable results. Source: Statements by Gabriel Avr ă mescu, First Vice-President of the Financial Supervisory Authority (ASF), as publicly reported by AGERPRES.
